name: Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling Leaks
blurb:
Direct-to-chip liquid cooling replaced air cooling because high-power accelerators generate more heat than air can carry away. That moved water and dielectric fluid inside the rack, alongside energised electrical equipment, and property underwriters are repricing the result.

Swiss Re put a number on it in July 2026. Reviewing fifteen years of data centre losses, liquid-related damage accounts for close to a quarter of total loss costs: roughly 9 percent from fire sprinkler leakage and about 10 percent from escaped liquid introduced by newer cooling systems. FM added a dedicated liquid-cooling section to its 2026 loss prevention guidance, which is the practical signal that underwriters have moved from watching this to pricing it.

The failure modes are not the ones property forms were written against. Improperly installed manifolds, maintenance error on pressurised coolant lines, and the interaction between a coolant leak and high-voltage equipment produce loss scenarios that pre-date nobody's actuarial tables because they did not previously exist at this density. A facility that converted from air to liquid mid-life carries a risk profile its policy may still describe in air-cooled terms.

points.desc: Swiss Re, reviewing fifteen years of losses in its July 2026 sigma insights on insuring AI, attributes close to 24 percent of total data centre loss costs to liquid: roughly 9 percent fire sprinkler leakage and about 10 percent escaped liquid from newer cooling systems.
points.name: Liquid losses are about a quarter of all data centre loss cost

points.desc: The 2026 loss prevention guidance adds a dedicated liquid-cooling section. Loss prevention standards are what underwriters attach conditions to, so a new section is usually the step before a new question on a renewal submission.
points.name: FM wrote a liquid cooling section into its 2026 guidance

points.desc: Standard property forms cover sudden and accidental water damage, which reaches most liquid cooling failures. The qualifier does the work: a slow seep or a corrosion-driven degradation may not be sudden, and that is where the argument happens.
points.name: Sudden and accidental water damage usually responds

points.desc: Where a coolant leak reaches energised high-voltage equipment the loss can fall to equipment breakdown rather than property. Brokers are advising that the policy name cooling system components explicitly rather than leaving the trigger to be argued after a loss.
points.name: Equipment breakdown has to name cooling components

points.desc: A facility that moves from air to liquid cooling changes its risk profile without changing its policy. Submissions written on air-cooled assumptions may not respond correctly to a liquid loss, which makes the conversion a re-underwriting event rather than a maintenance one.
points.name: A mid-life conversion can outrun its own policy

points.desc: General liability and property forms commonly carry pollution exclusions or narrow sublimits. Dielectric fluids, refrigerants and glycol are all contaminants, so environmental impairment cover is a separate purchase rather than something the property policy quietly includes.
points.name: Pollution exclusions sit underneath the coolant question

points.desc: Where the leak traces to a contractor manifold or a design decision, the response is professional liability on the designer or installer, not the operator property policy. Design-build arrangements expand that exposure well past standard general liability limits.
points.name: Installation and design error is a different policy

points.desc: The pattern after a loss class is recognised is an endorsement narrowing it. Worth watching carrier filings and Lloyds wordings for a named liquid-cooling exclusion or sublimit, which would be the clearest signal that the market has repriced this rather than absorbed it.
points.name: To verify: whether any carrier has filed a liquid-cooling exclusion

points.desc: Property covers the destroyed hardware. Equipment breakdown, sometimes still written as boiler and machinery, is the endorsement that reaches internal perils: a pump failure, a pressure rupture, an electrical short caused by the leak. An electronic data processing rider is what values accelerators at replacement cost rather than depreciated value, which on current GPU pricing is the difference that matters.
points.name: What responds: property plus an equipment breakdown endorsement

points.desc: Interruption cover commonly carries a 24 to 48 hour waiting period before it responds. For a training cluster that is the whole loss. Extra expense is the companion that pays for rushed replacement hardware, emergency technicians and rented compute while the room is down.
points.name: The business interruption waiting period is the clause to negotiate

points.desc: An operator or managed service provider whose leak takes down a customer workload faces a contract and damages claim, not a property claim. Technology errors and omissions is the line that answers it, and it is separate from the property and cyber towers.
points.name: Hosting somebody else changes which policy responds

points.desc: Accelsius launched NeuGuard in March 2025, underwritten by CNA, offering up to 100,000 dollars per rack for internal damage caused by a NeuCool leak, on two, three and five year terms, with SKU-level server warranties added through OEM partners. A vendor-backed guarantee sits ahead of the operator policy and is worth pricing into a cooling procurement rather than treating as marketing.
points.name: Vendor leak guarantees are becoming a first layer

points.desc: Where a defect caused the leak, the operator insurer pays and then pursues the integrator or manufacturer. That makes product liability the exposure on the other side of the same event, and design-build arrangements widen it well past standard general liability limits.
points.name: Subrogation runs back to the installer

summary: Liquid-related damage is close to a quarter of data centre loss costs over fifteen years, and direct-to-chip cooling put fluid next to energised equipment. What standard property forms cover, where equipment breakdown has to be named explicitly, and why a mid-life conversion can outrun its own policy wording.

children.desc: What carriers will actually write against a campus worth twenty to thirty billion, how towers are layered across forty or more carriers, and where the uninsured remainder lands.
children.name: Capacity and Layered Programs
